question: By what factor did the porosity of the Y1 cubic shale sample increase after 14 days of solvent extraction?
rendered:
<document title="Sequential Solvent Extraction Reveals Lithofacies-Dependent Pore Accessibility, Wettability, and Hydrocarbon Partitioning in Organic-Rich Lacustrine Shales">

=== page 3 ===
- Cubic samples were soaked in a beaker containing a dichloromethane/methanol solvent mixture at a volume ratio of 93:7.
- The DCM/MeOH mixture of 93:7 (v/v) was selected as a conventional and reproducible solvent system that can extract both nonpolar to moderately polar hydrocarbons and part of the polar compounds associated with mineral and organic surfaces.^39−41 The beaker was placed in a water bath at 40 °C for 14 days to remove the oil in the samples as a batch.
- The mixed fluids were changed every 2− 3 days to ensure a high solvent extraction efficiency.
- A total of 50 g of 20−35 mesh particles of each sample was prepared for sequential solvent extraction (Figure 2).
- The particle samples were placed in a cellulose cylinder filter and extracted with a mixed fluid of dichloromethane and methanol in a volume ratio of 93:7.
- The extraction durations were set at 1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 30, and 60 days, the residual solid samples were retained for MIP, NP, and CV− SANS experiments, and the extracted oils were collected for gas chromatography and SARA fractionation analyses.

=== page 4 ===
- In addition to the sequential solvent extraction, two supplementary extraction designs were conducted to evaluate the hydrocarbons remaining after the 60 day conventional extraction.
- In the first design, approximately 10 g of the residual solid samples after 60 days of extraction were collected and ball-milled to <300 mesh.
- The pulverized samples were then subjected to an additional 14 day conventional solvent extraction using the same DCM/MeOH mixture, and the oil obtained from this step was named D60-Powder.
- Subsequently, on day 200 after the initial extraction, the extracted pulverized residues were further treated by accelerated solvent extraction (ASE) using a Thermo Fisher ASE 350 system at 130 °C and 1500 psi for 30 min, and the oil collected from this step was named D200-Powder-ASE.
- In the second design, the residual 20−35 mesh samples after the 60 day sequential extraction were directly subjected to ASE on day 200 after the initial extraction without further pulverization.
- After solvent extraction, the porosity of the Y1 sample increased from 2.96% to 20.4%.

Answer: The porosity of the Y1 cubic shale sample increased by a factor of 6.86 (20.4/2.96).
